story.value: Titanium was discovered in 1791 by the Reverend William Gregor, an English pastor.
The name titanium comes from the Latin titans, the first sons of the Earth in Greek mythology.
In 1795, the German chemist Martin Heinrich Klaproth rediscovered the element and called it titanium.

uses.value: Because titanium does not react within the human body, it is used to make implants such as artificial hips and pins for setting bones.
Titanium oxide is used as a pigment to make white paint.
Titanium is used in parts of boats that are exposed to sea water, such as propeller shafts and rigging.
Titanium and titanium alloys are used in airplanes, among other things.
